terra.problem: The disciples report what people say; the passage does not say a crowd offered those guesses.
The joke places Nehemiah off working on his wall during this scene and suggests why he is absent from the list. The passage says neither.
The imagined quiet room and people staring at their shoes are presented as the scene. Jesus and His disciples are on the way.
The passage does not say anyone raised a hand.
The disciples report what people say; the passage does not say a crowd was handing out names.
The passage attributes those answers to people, not to a crowd.
The hypothetical “spread the word!” puts invented words in Jesus' mouth.
Taking Jesus aside does not establish that Peter spoke to Him privately.
The passage does not say people lean in, and it gives no reason for them to do so.
The passage does not say whether Jesus smiled.
The text does give a time boundary: some standing there will see the kingdom arrive with power before they taste death. Saying it does not say when overlooks that.
